chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no man who withholds a dirham of a right except that he spends two [dirhams] in what is not its right; and there is no man who withholds a right in his wealth except that Allah collars him with it, a snake of fire, on the Day of Resurrection.'

He said: I said to him, 'A man who is knowledgeable paid his Zakat to other than its rightful recipients for a period. Is it upon him to pay it a second time to its rightful recipients when he knows them?' He said: 'Yes.'

He said: I said, 'And if he did not know its rightful recipients so he did not pay it, or he did not know that it was upon him, and then he learned of that?' He said: 'He should pay it to its rightful recipients for what has passed.'

He said: I said to him, 'Suppose he did not know its rightful recipients, so he gave it to one who was not deserving of it, and he had sought and exerted himself, then he learned afterwards the evil of what he had done.' He said: 'It is not upon him to pay it another time.'
And from Zurara, similar to it, except that he said: 'If he exerted himself, then he is blameless; and if he was deficient in the exertion regarding the seeking, then no.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zakat paid to the wrong recipients if the payer made a sincere effort to find the correct ones?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the conditions under which Zakat must be repaid if given to non-Ahl al-Wilayah, distinguishing between negligence and sincere effort (ijtihad). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific eligibility of the 'poor' and 'needy' as those who possess knowledge of the Imam, linking financial purification to spiritual allegiance. The text further illustrates the principle of divine mercy, where unintentional error or lack of knowledge exempts the payer from double payment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdllah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from a man who prevent a Dirham from a right except that he would spend two in other than its rightful way; and there is none from a man who prevents a right in his wealth except that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Collar him, due to it, a snake of fire on the Day of Judgement’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘An understanding man paid his Zakāt to other than its deserving ones for a long time. Would it be upon him that he repeats it for a second time to its deserving ones when he does know them?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.

I said, ‘Supposing he does not recognise its deserving ones so he does not give it, or does not know that is it upon him (to give), so he comes to know after that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should pay it to its deserving ones of what has passed’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Supposing he did not know its deserving ones, so he handed it over to the one who was not deserving of it, and he had sought and strived, then came to know after that, the evil of what he had done’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not upon him that he pays it another time’.

And from Zurara, similar to it, apart from that, that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he had strived, so he is blameless, and if he was deficient in the striving regarding the seeking (of the deserving recipient), so no’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Whoever withholds one dirham of right, he ends up spending two dirhams for the cause of falsehood. If one denies payment of one dirham of right on his wealth, Allah makes a snake of fire to curl around him on the Day of Judgment.’

He (the narrator) has said that he asked about a man who is knowledgeable, but has paid his Zakat to undeserving people at a certain time has he to pay it again to the deserving people if he knows them? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he is required to do so.’

I then asked, ‘What should he do if he does not find any deserving people? Thus he did not pay, or he did not know if he owes anything or not, but later finds out that he owes.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to pay to the deserving people for the past.’

I then asked, ‘What is he required to do if he does not find the deserving people and pays to undeserving people although he had done his best and then found out bad things that he had done.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is not required to pay it one more time.’”

Zurarah has narrated a similar Hadith, except that if he does his best he becomes free of his responsibility, but if he has fallen short in doing his best to find out proper beneficiary, then he is not free of his responsibility.”
